rituals.name: Ganesh Puja
rituals.subtitle: Invocation of Lord Ganesha for Obstacle-Free Celebrations
rituals.significance: Invoking Lord Ganesha, the remover of all obstacles (Vighnaharta), to bless the couple and ensure harmony throughout the wedding celebrations.
rituals.dressCode: Traditional Indian attire in bright yellow, orange, or gold.

dos: Remove footwear before entering the puja mandap
donts: Avoid black or dark gray clothing during auspicious pujas

rituals.guestNotes: A serene, sacred ceremony where close family and elders sit together with the priest.

rituals.name: Haldi & Pithi Ceremony
rituals.subtitle: Purification & Golden Glow Ritual
rituals.significance: Applying an auspicious paste of turmeric, sandalwood, and rosewater onto the bride and groom. Turmeric possesses antiseptic qualities and imparts a radiant glow while shielding from evil eyes (Nazar).
rituals.dressCode: Yellow or mustard ethnic wear that you don't mind getting stained with turmeric!

dos: Prepare for music, laughter, and flower petal showers
donts: Do not leave the house alone after Haldi as per ancient custom

rituals.guestNotes: One of the most fun and photogenic rituals! Everyone takes turns dabbing turmeric paste on the couple's face, hands, and feet.

rituals.name: Mehndi & Sangeet Night
rituals.subtitle: Henna Artwork & Musical Extravaganza
rituals.significance: Intricate henna designs symbolize fertility, love, and good fortune; the darker the stain, the deeper the love. The Sangeet celebrates the union with coordinated dance performances from both families.
rituals.dressCode: Teal, emerald green, royal purple, or floral lehengas and kurtas.

dos: Join in the dance floor and cheering for family performances
Let henna dry naturally for 6-8 hours
donts: Do not wash fresh henna with soap and water on the first night

rituals.guestNotes: High energy celebration! Professional henna artists will be available for all guests to receive complementary henna designs.

rituals.name: Baraat & Milni
rituals.subtitle: Groom's Grand Procession & Family Greeting
rituals.significance: The groom arrives in a royal procession on a decorated horse or vintage convertible with live dhol drummers. At the venue entrance, Milni takes place where corresponding male relatives from both sides embrace and exchange floral garlands.
rituals.dressCode: Formal sherwanis, bandhgalas, or heavy silk sarees with safa (turbans).

dos: Wear the ceremonial safa/pagdi provided at the gate
donts: Do not block the entrance path for the bride's welcoming party

rituals.guestNotes: A pulsating street party with live drums leading right to the ceremonial gateway.

rituals.name: Saat Phere & Kanyadaan
rituals.subtitle: Seven Sacred Vows Around the Holy Agni
rituals.significance: The heart of the Hindu wedding. The bride's parents offer their blessings (Kanyadaan). The couple circles the sacred fire (Agni) seven times, sealing vows of food, strength, prosperity, happiness, progeny, longevity, and eternal friendship.
rituals.dressCode: Regal wedding attire: Red, Maroon, Rust, or Ivory with Gold accents.

dos: Maintain silence during the Sanskrit Vedic chants
Shower flower petals during the Phere
donts: Do not step onto the elevated sacred mandap platform unless invited by the pandit

rituals.guestNotes: The Sanskrit verses will be translated into English by the priest so all guests can appreciate their poetic vows.

rituals.name: Anand Karaj (Laavan)
rituals.subtitle: Blissful Union in the Presence of Sri Guru Granth Sahib
rituals.significance: The Sikh holy marriage ceremony performed inside the Gurdwara. The couple walks around the Sri Guru Granth Sahib four times as the four Laavan hymns are sung, signifying spiritual awakening, yearning, restraint, and divine union.
rituals.dressCode: Modest traditional attire. Both men and women MUST cover their heads (rumal/chunni) and remove shoes.

dos: Cover your head before entering the Darbar Sahib
Sit cross-legged respectfully on the carpeted floor
donts: Never point your feet directly toward the Sri Guru Granth Sahib
No smoking, tobacco, or alcohol allowed on premises

rituals.guestNotes: Followed by Guru ka Langar—a community meal served to everyone sitting together as equals regardless of religion or background.

rituals.name: Exchange of Vows & Rings
rituals.subtitle: Solemn Covenant of Love & Unity
rituals.significance: The exchange of personalized vows promising lifelong fidelity and love, sealed with the exchange of wedding bands symbolizing endless commitment without beginning or end.
rituals.dressCode: Formal western: Tuxedos, suits, evening gowns, or cocktail dresses.
itemsNeeded: Unity candle or sand ceremony set

dos: Arrive 15 minutes before the processional begins
Silence all mobile devices during readings
donts: Do not stand in the central aisle during the bride's walk

rituals.guestNotes: Includes the lighting of the Unity Candle or blending of sands to symbolize two separate lives becoming one.

rituals.name: Nikah Ceremony
rituals.subtitle: Sacred Marriage Contract & Ijab-o-Qubool
rituals.significance: The signing of the official Islamic marriage contract in the presence of the Qazi and witnesses. Both bride and groom express free consent by uttering 'Qubool Hai' (I accept) three times, with agreed upon Mahr (gift of protection).
rituals.dressCode: Elegant modest festive attire: Shararas, Ghararas, Sherwanis.

dos: Offer heartfelt Duas and Mubarak to the newly wedded couple
Adhere to the venue's modesty guidelines
donts: Avoid noisy interruptions while the Qazi recites the Khutbah

rituals.guestNotes: Followed by Arsi Mushaf—where the couple shares their first glimpse through a decorative mirror.
